findings.claim: The model answer says rebêche belongs to 'Champagne, not Burgundy', and the accept list only takes answers that deny Burgundy.
findings.finalFix: q: "Explain 'rebêche': what is it, and in which region did the term originate?" ans: "Champagne: the final press fraction after the cuvée and taille, excluded from the appellation and sent to distillation; Crémant de Bourgogne also regulates it (a rebêche rate of 0 to 10% of settled must)" accept: ["~champagne", "champagne final press fraction", "champagne term last press fraction", "champagne pressing final cut"] exp: "Rebêche is a Champagne pressing term for the last, harshest juice, which may not be made into appellation wine. Burgundy uses it too: the Crémant de Bourgogne cahier des charges (homologated 2 December 2021) sets a rebêche rate of 0 to 10% of settled must, requires new press sites to fractionate into cuvées, tailles and rebêches, and has rebêche volumes recorded in the press book."

findings.claim: The stem asks for the 'current legal curiosity', and the answer says de Vogüé's Musigny Blanc has been declassified to Bourgogne Blanc since 1994, still in the present tense.
findings.finalFix: q: "Give the appellation and producer of 'Musigny Blanc', and the legal curiosity of its 1994 to 2014 vintages." ans: "Musigny Grand Cru (Chambolle-Musigny), Comte Georges de Vogüé, the only white Musigny; its 1994 to 2014 vintages were voluntarily declassified to Bourgogne Blanc while replanted vines matured, and it returned as Musigny Blanc Grand Cru with the 2015 vintage" accept: ["de vogue bourgogne blanc", "vogue declassified to bourgogne blanc", "vogue bourgogne blanc until 2015"] exp: "A grand cru estate voluntarily labelling its wine as regional for 21 vintages, a paradox Masters love; the Grand Cru label returned in 2015."

findings.claim: The model answer says Clos de Bèze may be labelled 'Chambertin' 'under the 1936 decree'.
findings.finalFix: ans: "The Abbey of Bèze planted it c. 630, the oldest documented Burgundy cru; under the 1937 decree it may be labelled simply 'Chambertin', though Chambertin may never be sold as Clos de Bèze"

findings.finalFix: list: 1, items: ["Abbey of Bèze (Bèze)", "630 (7th century)", "Chambertin"], need: 3, accept: ["abbey of beze 630 chambertin"], ans: "Abbey of Bèze, c. 630, Chambertin", exp: "Duke Amalgaire gave the land to the Abbey of Bèze c. 630, which makes Clos de Bèze the oldest documented Burgundy cru. findings.claim: The model answer says AOC wines 'must pass the agrément — an analytical and tasting approval', and that failing it means declassification.
findings.finalFix: ans: "Since the 2008 INAO reform every operator must hold a habilitation and follow the appellation's control plan; independent inspection bodies (OI/OC) run analytical and tasting checks on samples. A failed product check means the wine is downgraded, and repeated failure or a breach of the cahier des charges can cost the operator its habilitation, and with it the right to the name. (Before 2008 this was the systematic agrément.)" Add accept entries "~habilitation", "~product control" and "~failed control", and keep the agrément entries as historical answers.
